# Vendor KaTeX Instead of CDN

**Decision.** Copy [[katex]] — `katex.min.js`, `katex.min.css`, `auto-render.min.js` and all 20
`KaTeX_*.woff2` font files — into `exam_prep/vendor/katex/` and load them by relative path, rather
than linking a CDN build.

**Date.** The vendored files carry the earliest mtimes in [[physics-exam-prep]], 2026-06-27; first
committed 2026-07-10.

## Why

The requirement is stated as the app's headline, not as a footnote:

> "No build step. No server. No internet. **Open one HTML file and start revising.**"
> — Physics/README.md, 2026-07-10

and the vendored folder is annotated with the consequence:

> "        └── katex/                  # bundled KaTeX (offline math) — no CDN needed"
> — Physics/exam_prep/snapshot.md, 2026-06-30

The failure a CDN would cause is specific to this deliverable: a study app is used the night before
an exam, plausibly with no connection, and math that fails to render is not degraded output — it is
a blank formula where the answer should be. Fonts make it worse than a normal CDN dependency,
because `katex.min.css` references 20 font files, so a partially-cached CDN load renders text with
the wrong glyphs rather than failing cleanly.

## Alternatives rejected

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| **KaTeX from a CDN** | needs the network at exactly the moment the app promises not to; the CSS pulls 20 fonts, so partial failure is silent and ugly |
| **MathJax** (vendored or CDN) | heavier, asynchronous, and its extra LaTeX coverage buys nothing for a physics syllabus. **TODO:** never actually compared in-repo — see below |
| **Pre-render formulas to images** | breaks selection, scaling and dark mode; the knowledge base stores math as `\(…\)` strings and renders them at runtime |
| **Install via npm and bundle** | would introduce the `package.json` and build step the whole app exists without — [[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] |

**TODO:** the KaTeX-vs-MathJax comparison above is reconstructed engineering reasoning, **not a
recorded rationale.** No file in the repo weighs the two, and it was not asked at interview.
`confidence: low` on why KaTeX specifically; `high` on the vendoring decision and its stated reason.

## What makes it hold

Vendoring alone would not guarantee the offline promise — the service worker still has to precache
the files. All 23 KaTeX assets are listed in `sw.js`'s `CORE` array, and `tools/qa.mjs` check 8
fails if anything `index.html` loads is missing from that list. The install strategy that keeps a
single missing file from aborting the whole cache is [[cache-individually-not-addall]].

## Cost, stated plainly

~304 KB of JS/CSS plus 20 font files committed permanently, with **no version pin and no update
path recorded anywhere**. The copy is frozen at whatever was current on 2026-06-27. For a frozen
coursework artefact that is the right trade; for anything maintained it is a silent staleness debt.

The same instinct appears one repo over as [[vendor-react-over-babel-cdn]], where the CDN was not a
risk but an observed failure — a blank page under `file://`. Two repos, same conclusion, reached
from opposite directions: [[physics-exam-prep]] vendored pre-emptively,
[[discrete-mathematics-laboratories]] vendored after being burned.
